title: Madheads
blurb: An R&D project built at Manchester Innovation Lab, testing how playful machine vision can turn a passing crowd into a collective portrait.

title: TILO v2
blurb: The second generation of TILO, our hybrid display system for arts and cultural venues — digital public space that holds a personalised, emotional dialogue with visitors.

title: Fantasia Express
commissioner: Innovate UK — First of a Kind
blurb: Twelve months of R&D into location-based augmented reality inside a moving train carriage, trialled for two weeks between London and Newcastle. Or: an alien spaceship sent to collect relics of our imagination.
credits: With LNER, Corporation Pop and Immersive Storylab

title: BIGMOUTH
blurb: A cross between a confessional and Room 101. People told the BIGMOUTH what was wrong with the world, then watched through an eyepiece as their words became the mouth of a small demon that carried the burden away.
credits: Demon illustrations by Tomo. Spherical projection with Pufferfish Displays

title: Cakenocake
blurb: A weekend on Liverpool high street with a signboard and no technology at all. Every question had two answers, and which side of the street you walked was how you gave yours.

title: Emofie
blurb: Selfies crossed with emojis — a mobile app and a gallery installation in one. Strangers perform an emotion for the camera, make something daft with it, and walk on.

title: When I Grow Up
blurb: Children picked a future self on an iPad and watched a hand-drawn avatar of it mirror their movements across the cafe video wall — then left it behind for the next visitor to wear.

title: TILO
commissioner: Digital R&D Fund for the Arts
blurb: A hybrid display system for cultural venues, and an attempt to make the screens in an arts building talk back — personalised, contextual, and aware of the weather outside.
credits: With Amaze and Pixel Inspiration. Research by the Creative Exchange, Lancaster University

title: The Humble Market
blurb: Lead artists on a collaboration between four Brazilian and UK artists — a trading floor for things that can't be traded, staged at FACT, under a railway arch in Preston, and at the 2014 World Cup.

title: MeYouAndUs
commissioner: FACT · BBC Big Screens · Robots and Avatars
blurb: The series the practice is named after. A set of adaptable interactive artworks that ran on BBC big screens in three cities, in a Brazilian town square, and in a touring European exhibition.

title: Not the Beatles Tour
blurb: A walking tour of Liverpool that refuses to mention the obvious — the city's other stories, triggered by location on people's own phones as they walk.

title: Homewalk
blurb: A walk between where you are and where home is, made with people who have made that journey the hard way.

title: Kindred Spirits
blurb: An evening takeover of Tate Liverpool built from Mondrian. Visitors chose a colour, made a costume, sat for a photobooth, and found themselves on a wall of thirty-six screens beside everyone who chose the same.
credits: With Tate Collective and the Costumologists. Audio by Kepla

title: Sonic Market
blurb: Every hour the market's own sounds are collected, bent by live weather data, and returned quietly to the space that made them — turning the whole market into an unpredictable instrument.

title: Invisible Arts Network
blurb: A six-month residency mapping the art already happening in a county that doesn't call it art, launched with The Happening — a day conference that turned into a psychedelic party with 360 cinema and VR.

title: Handprint 2012
blurb: Online interventions and live events across the North West, ending with four projectors throwing hundreds of scanned hands onto a railway bridge in Avenham Park — where they appeared to rise out of the water.
credits: Part of WE PLAY, the North West's London 2012 legacy programme

blurb: A permanent installation in a health centre waiting room. Seventy-two local people filmed waiting at bus stops on hot summer days, playing to the people waiting inside — bus routes as the arteries of a community.
credits: Community engagement led by tenantspin with ABCC

title: Wishing Well
blurb: A permanent interactive installation in the courtyard garden of a new-build health centre, made through community workshops as part of Liverpool's Decade of Health and Wellbeing.

title: Lowry to Life
blurb: Two linked installations on opposite sides of the city, built from L.S. Lowry's 1954 painting of Piccadilly Gardens, made to mark the University of Salford's move to MediaCityUK.

title: Handprint
blurb: Four nights of live hand projection onto Manchester's second tallest building. The first Handprint, and the work the 2012 Cultural Olympiad commission grew out of.
